courses.title: Slice
courses.description: Learn Slice for Excel, one short lesson a day.

units.title: Slice basics
units.objective: Understand what Slice is, what it needs to connect to TM1, and how the Community and Business editions differ.

sources.title: Getting Started with Slice – Installation and Connection

lessons.title: What is Slice?
lessons.tip: Slice is an Excel add-in that connects Excel to TM1 through the TM1 REST API.

exercises.q: What is Slice?
options: A Microsoft Excel add-in for TM1
A standalone web browser for TM1
A replacement for the TM1 server
exercises.explain: Slice is an Excel add-in for IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), similar to Perspectives and PAfE.

exercises.q: Slice connects directly to the TM1 ___ API.
exercises.explain: All Slice operations use the TM1 REST API instead of the legacy Perspectives C API.

exercises.q: Slice works with existing reports built in Perspectives.
exercises.explain: Slice supports reports built in Perspectives and in formula mode in PA for Excel.

exercises.q: Match each part of Slice to what it does
exercises.explain: Slice has two main parts: the Excel Add-in and the Server Explorer, which includes the Cube Viewer and Subset Editor.

exercises.q: Slice has built-in support for TM1 hierarchies.
exercises.explain: Hierarchy support is built in, so you can create slices and Active Forms with hierarchies.

lessons.title: Installing and connecting
lessons.tip: Slice needs TM1 11 or later with the REST API enabled, and it connects to TM1 through Arc.

exercises.q: Which TM1 version does Slice require?
exercises.explain: TM1 11 or later is required, since many important APIs only exist from TM1 11.

exercises.q: Slice must be installed on each user's own computer.
exercises.explain: It is an Excel add-in installed per PC, and all users can connect to one central Arc server.

exercises.q: Run the Slice installer as ___.
exercises.explain: The quick start says to run slice.x.x.x.exe as Administrator.

exercises.q: Put the quick start steps in order
items: Download Slice from the Cubewise website
Open Slice 32-bit or 64-bit to match Excel
Click Servers in the Slice Ribbon
exercises.explain: Download, install, open the right version, then click Servers to find your TM1 instances.

exercises.q: Can't connect? Which part of your login is case-sensitive?
exercises.explain: When checking credentials, remember the CAM Namespace is case-sensitive.

lessons.title: Community vs Business
lessons.tip: Community gives you the classic Perspectives features plus hierarchies; Business adds support and advanced features.

exercises.q: The Community edition requires a subscription.
exercises.explain: Community is available without a subscription. Business requires one.

exercises.q: Which feature is only in the Business edition?
exercises.explain: MDX Forms are a Business feature. The others are already in Community.

exercises.q: Match each Business feature to what it does
pairs: Pastes values over DBRW without losing formulas
Explains why a cell has an error
Lets you share a sheet with people without TM1
Creates output files driven by a subset or MDX
exercises.explain: These are all Business edition features listed in the editions comparison.

exercises.q: Annotations, Sandboxes and Trace Rules are in the ___ edition.
exercises.explain: They are Community features, and Business includes everything in Community.

exercises.q: The Business edition includes product support from Cubewise.
exercises.explain: Business adds commercial support through the Cubewise service desk.

units.title: The Slice ribbon
units.objective: Find your way around the Slice ribbon: refresh or rebuild sheets and export a cube view to Excel.

lessons.title: Refresh vs rebuild
lessons.tip: SHIFT+F9 calculates the sheet, ALT+F9 rebuilds Active Forms, and F9 calculates all sheets.

exercises.q: Match each shortcut to its action
pairs: Rebuild the Active Form on the sheet
exercises.explain: These are the Refresh Sheet, Rebuild Sheet and Refresh Book shortcuts.

exercises.q: By default, Slice turns off Excel's automatic recalculation.
exercises.explain: Slice disables automatic recalculation by default, so you refresh when you need to.

exercises.q: You typed a new formula but it doesn't update. What do you do?
options: Press SHIFT+F9 to refresh the sheet
exercises.explain: With automatic recalculation off, click Refresh Sheet or press SHIFT+F9.

exercises.q: Rebuild Book rebuilds all ___ in the workbook.
exercises.explain: Rebuild Book rebuilds every Active Form in the workbook.

exercises.q: Where do you switch between manual and auto calculation?
exercises.explain: Settings holds the TM1 connection and features like manual or auto calculation.

lessons.title: Ribbon buttons tour
lessons.tip: Each ribbon button has one job, from uploading reports to managing sandboxes.

exercises.q: Match each button to what it does
pairs: Uploads the workbook to the TM1 application folder
Creates, resets or commits a sandbox
Shows all actions taken by Slice
exercises.explain: Each of these buttons sits on the Slice tab of the ribbon.

exercises.q: Which button shows stats like the number of TM1 formulas?
exercises.explain: Audit gives statistics on the file, such as how many TM1 formulas it has.

exercises.q: Add Button can create a button that executes a TM1 process.
exercises.explain: Action Buttons can calculate the workbook, execute a process or open a workbook from the application folder.

exercises.q: The Report Burster exports to Excel or ___ files.
exercises.explain: It bursts a report to single or multiple Excel or PDF files by cycling through a subset.

exercises.q: Which shortcut shows or hides the Slice Explorer's left-side menu?
exercises.explain: CTRL+SHIFT+M toggles the menu to give you more workspace.

lessons.title: Export a view to Excel
lessons.tip: Exporting a view as a Slice puts DBRW formulas in the data area and SUBNM formulas in the titles.

exercises.q: Put the export steps in order
items: Click Server Explorer in the Slice Ribbon
Open a view of a cube
Select New Workbook and click OK
exercises.explain: The view lands in a new workbook, built with TM1 formulas.

exercises.q: In an exported Slice, which formulas fill the data area?
exercises.explain: The data area contains DBRW formulas.

exercises.q: The title area of an exported Slice uses ___ formulas.
exercises.explain: Titles are SUBNM formulas, so you can pick other elements.

exercises.q: A Slice is the same as a Custom Report in Planning Analytics for Excel.
exercises.explain: The manual describes a Slice as the equivalent of a PAfE Custom Report.

exercises.q: What does Convert TM1 Functions > This Worksheet do?
options: Removes TM1 formulas, keeps Excel formulas
Turns Excel formulas into TM1 ones
exercises.explain: After converting, only your Excel formulas stay in the sheet.

units.title: Worksheet formulas
units.objective: Read and write TM1 data with worksheet formulas such as DBRW, SUBNM and DBSW, and automate them with VBA.

lessons.title: Core TM1 formulas
lessons.tip: DBRW reads and writes cube values, SUBNM picks an element and DBRA reads an attribute.

exercises.q: Match each formula to its job
pairs: Returns an element from a hierarchy
Gets an attribute of an element
exercises.explain: These come from the Slice Worksheet Formulas reference.

exercises.q: Which formula writes a value to a cube?
exercises.explain: DBSW writes a value to a cube.

exercises.q: DIMSIZ returns the ___ of a hierarchy.
exercises.explain: DIMSIZ returns hierarchy size. DFRST gives the first element and DNLEV the number of levels.

exercises.q: DBSA sets an attribute value in a dimension.
exercises.explain: DBSA takes a value, Server:Dimension, element and attribute name.

exercises.q: What does ELPAR return?
options: The n-th parent of an element
The n-th child of an element
exercises.explain: ELPAR returns a parent. ELCOMP returns a child and ELLEV the level.

lessons.title: Sending data with DBS and DBSW
lessons.tip: Prefer DBSW over DBS, then press DBS Send to push your edits to TM1.

exercises.q: DBSW is significantly faster than DBS.
exercises.explain: The manual highly recommends DBSW instead of DBS wherever possible.

exercises.q: Put the recommended workflow in order
items: Click Refresh Sheet to update DBR/DBRW values
Edit the cells with DBS/DBSW formulas
Press DBS Send to push data to TM1
exercises.explain: Refresh first, edit, then send.

exercises.q: The ribbon's DBS Send button sends data for...
exercises.explain: No setting changes that button to work across the whole workbook.

exercises.q: A named range called ___ set to 1 sends DBS data on every refresh or rebuild.
exercises.explain: From Slice v4.6.1, SLICEDBSSEND = 1 makes DBS/DBSW fire on Refresh or Rebuild.

exercises.q: The DBS Send Data on Recalc setting applies to all users.
exercises.explain: It is stored locally and only applies to the machine where it is set.

lessons.title: Automating with VBA
lessons.tip: Slice's VBA functions run with Application.Run and can sit behind Excel buttons.

exercises.q: Call Slice VBA functions with Application.___.
exercises.explain: For example: Application.Run "TM1RECALC1".

exercises.q: Match each VBA function to what it does
pairs: Rebuilds all worksheets in the workbook
Sends DBS data for the whole workbook
exercises.explain: DBSSEND does the same as DBSSENDALL but only for the active sheet.

exercises.q: Which function runs a TurboIntegrator process?
exercises.explain: RunTIProcess executes a TM1 TI process from VBA or a worksheet.

exercises.q: N_CONNECT needs a CAM Namespace only when you use CAM authentication.
exercises.explain: The CAM Namespace parameter is optional and only required for CAM.

exercises.q: With Arc Server Groups, how do you name the server in N_CONNECT?
exercises.explain: Include the group, for example "Production:MyServer".

units.title: Active Forms
units.objective: Build Active Forms that expand with your TM1 data, write values back with Paste Range, and drill across dimensions.

sources.title: How to Create and Use Active Forms
Create an Active Form from Excel

lessons.title: Create an Active Form
lessons.tip: Active Forms are dynamic reports whose rows expand and collapse based on TM1 data.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Right-click a cell and open the Slice menu
Choose Active Form, then Insert Active Form
Pick the server, cube, view and type, then OK
exercises.explain: This inserts a new Active Form right from Excel.

exercises.q: You can also create an Active Form by exporting a view from the cube view.
exercises.explain: Open the view and export it as an Active Form.

exercises.q: Which button shows the hidden format area of an Active Form?
exercises.explain: Toggle it on to set number formats, then toggle it back to hidden.

exercises.q: After changing the format area, press ___ to rebuild the sheet.
exercises.explain: ALT+F9 is Rebuild Sheet.

exercises.q: Which function defines a master row in an Active Form?
exercises.explain: TM1RptRow defines the master row, and TM1RptView defines the view.

lessons.title: Writing back with Paste Range
lessons.tip: Paste Range pastes a block of values over DBRW cells and sends them to TM1, keeping the formulas.

exercises.q: Put the Paste Range steps in order
items: Type a value in one cell, e.g. 50
Select the rest of the row
Click Paste Range in the Slice Ribbon
exercises.explain: The values are sent to the TM1 server in one go.

exercises.q: After Paste Range, the cells lose their DBRW formulas.
exercises.explain: Each cell keeps its DBRW formula.

exercises.q: Why use Paste Range?
options: To send many values at once, not cell by cell
exercises.explain: It saves you typing values one cell at a time.

exercises.q: Paste Range pastes values over ___ formulas to upload data to TM1.
exercises.explain: It targets DBRW and DBR formulas.

exercises.q: DBS Send sends DBS values without refreshing the whole sheet.
exercises.explain: DBS Send triggers DBS functions without a full worksheet refresh.

lessons.title: Dynamic columns and Cross Drill
lessons.tip: Dynamic columns let columns expand and collapse too, and Cross Drill lets you drill into another dimension.

exercises.q: Which function drives dynamic columns?
exercises.explain: TM1RptColumn works like TM1RptRow, but for columns.

exercises.q: Click the ___ sign next to a consolidated column to expand it.
exercises.explain: Click + to expand and - to collapse, just like rows.

exercises.q: Active Forms with dynamic columns also work in TM1 Web.
exercises.explain: This is a Slice feature that TM1 Web does not support.

exercises.q: What does Cross Drill let you do in an Active Form?
options: Drill from one dimension into another
exercises.explain: For example, drill from Account into Region instead of only expanding Account.

exercises.q: Paste Range, Annotations and Cell Audit still work with dynamic columns.
exercises.explain: All other Active Form features work exactly as in a standard Active Form.

units.title: Right-click tools and auditing
units.objective: Use the right-click menu, annotations and audits to understand, comment on and check the numbers in your sheets.

sources.title: How to Create and Use Active Forms
Custom Audit Rules in Slice: Enhancements in Arc & Slice v6.1

lessons.title: The right-click menu
lessons.tip: Right-click a data cell to reach Slice tools like Trace Rules, Drill Through and Annotations.

exercises.q: Match each menu option to what it does
pairs: Shows how a cell's value is calculated
Drills to a cube, set up by an admin
exercises.explain: All of these are in the Slice context menu on a cell.

exercises.q: Which menu option spreads values?
exercises.explain: Data Spread is the option for spreading values.

exercises.q: Drill Through works without any setup by an administrator.
exercises.explain: Drill Through needs to be set up by an administrator first.

exercises.q: Cross Drill temporarily adds a new ___.
exercises.explain: The context menu describes Cross Drill as adding a new hierarchy temporarily.

exercises.q: How do you open the Slice context menu?
exercises.explain: Right-click a cell, then go to the Slice menu.

lessons.title: Annotations and Cell Audit
lessons.tip: Annotations save comments in TM1 for everyone, and Cell Audit explains why a formula fails.

exercises.q: Add an annotation
items: Click Add and write your comment
exercises.explain: The comment is written directly to the TM1 server.

exercises.q: Annotations are stored in your Excel file and only you can see them.
exercises.explain: Annotations are saved on the TM1 Server and visible to all users.

exercises.q: What does Cell Audit show?
options: Each element, its dimension and if the intersection is valid
exercises.explain: It shows the cube, dimension, hierarchy and element a cell refers to.

exercises.q: Cell Audit is especially handy when a formula returns a ___ error.
exercises.explain: Right-click the #VALUE! cell, then Slice > Cell Audit.

exercises.q: You type VarX in the Version cell. What happens?
exercises.explain: VarX is an invalid reference, and Cell Audit points to the Version dimension.

lessons.title: Best-practice audits
lessons.tip: Slice's audit flags common formula problems, and from v6.1 admins can add their own rules.

exercises.q: Which problem does the built-in best practice audit flag?
options: Several DBRW functions in one cell
exercises.explain: It also flags DBR used instead of DBRW and duplicate SUBNMs.

exercises.q: Custom audit rules live in the ___ file on the Arc server.
exercises.explain: Slice downloads bestpractices.yml from Arc every time a user runs an audit.

exercises.q: Each user must install the custom rules on their own PC.
exercises.explain: Rules live on the Arc server, so nothing is installed on users' machines.

exercises.q: Match each audit action to its result
pairs: Lists best practice violations for the sheet
Click a finding in the Reviewer
exercises.explain: Both audit tools are on the Slice ribbon.

exercises.q: If Arc can't be reached, the audit still runs the built-in rules.
exercises.explain: Only built-in rules run, and the audit says custom rules were not checked.

units.title: Aggregating on the fly
units.objective: Add up data on the fly with virtual consolidations, virtual expressions and the other ways DBRW can aggregate.

sources.title: 5 Ways to Aggregate Data with Slice

lessons.title: Virtual Consolidations
lessons.tip: A Virtual Consolidation adds up several elements on the fly, without changing the TM1 model.

exercises.q: Which prefix marks a Virtual Consolidation?
exercises.explain: A single # marks a Virtual Consolidation, for example #VIC+QLD+Tasmania.

exercises.q: Create a Virtual Consolidation
items: Double-click a cell with a SUBNM formula
exercises.explain: Holding CTRL lets you pick several elements in the Subset Editor.

exercises.q: Virtual Consolidations can only add elements, not subtract them.
exercises.explain: Sum is the default, but -, * and / also work.

exercises.q: In #3+5, the numbers 3 and 5 are element ___.
exercises.explain: 3 is the index for England and 5 for Scotland.

exercises.q: How do you show the variance between England (3) and Scotland (5)?
exercises.explain: Change the operator from + to - and refresh the sheet.

lessons.title: Virtual Expressions and ranges
lessons.tip: Start a cell with ## to run MDX functions like AVG or MAX right in your sheet.

exercises.q: A Virtual Expression starts with ___.
exercises.explain: ## is followed by the function name and an MDX set.

exercises.q: Which is a valid Virtual Expression?
exercises.explain: This averages VIC and NSW directly in the cell.

exercises.q: Virtual Expressions are calculated by the TM1 server.
exercises.explain: They run on the TM1 server as part of the MDX query Slice generates.

exercises.q: Named range myRegions holds VIC, QLD and Tasmania. What does DBRW return with it?
options: The sum of the three regions
exercises.explain: Slice aggregates all elements in the named range.

exercises.q: Match each Virtual Expression function to its result
exercises.explain: These are some of the MDX functions you can use in a Virtual Expression.

lessons.title: Five ways to aggregate with DBRW
lessons.tip: DBRW can aggregate through consolidations, subsets, virtual consolidations, virtual expressions or cell ranges.

exercises.q: Match each method to how it aggregates
pairs: Sums all elements in a subset
Uses elements listed in Excel cells
exercises.explain: Pick the method that fits your report.

exercises.q: Subset references came back from Perspectives in Slice v___.
exercises.explain: Slice v4.6.0 brought subset references back from TM1 Perspectives.

exercises.q: Virtual Consolidations require a change to the TM1 model.
exercises.explain: They aggregate elements on the fly without modifying the model.

exercises.q: Which method suits custom averages or ratios?
exercises.explain: Virtual Expressions combine DBRW with MDX functions for custom roll-ups.

exercises.q: Which method is handy for flexible ad hoc reports?
exercises.explain: Cell range references are especially useful for ad hoc reports.

units.title: Hierarchies
units.objective: Point your formulas and Active Forms at alternate hierarchies with SUBNM and DBHW.

sources.title: Using Hierarchies in DBH and DBHW Formulas

lessons.title: Hierarchies in SUBNM
lessons.tip: Add :HierarchyName after the dimension name to point a SUBNM at another hierarchy.

exercises.q: In TM1, one dimension can contain several hierarchies.
exercises.explain: For example, Region can have a Default and a Currency hierarchy.

exercises.q: =SUBNM("TM1SRV01:Region:___","Default","3","Description") uses the Currency hierarchy.
exercises.explain: The hierarchy name goes after the dimension name.

exercises.q: What happens when you double-click a SUBNM formula?
exercises.explain: With a hierarchy in the formula, you see that hierarchy's elements.

exercises.q: Show and use hierarchies in the Cube Viewer
items: Toggle the View Hierarchy Panel button
Drag the hierarchy to the titles area
exercises.explain: Then export the view to Excel as a Slice.

exercises.q: One report can use both the Default and Currency hierarchies of a dimension.
exercises.explain: Put them in separate cells, pick elements and refresh to compare.

lessons.title: DBHW and Active Forms
lessons.tip: Slice writes DBHW instead of DBRW automatically when a view uses hierarchies.

exercises.q: When does Slice generate DBHW instead of DBRW?
exercises.explain: Export a hierarchy-aware view and Slice handles it for you.

exercises.q: Match each formula to its role
pairs: Active Form row that can use a hierarchy
exercises.explain: All of them use the same :HierarchyName syntax.

exercises.q: If a hierarchy isn't referenced in DBHW, the default member is used.
exercises.explain: You don't need to include every hierarchy.

exercises.q: The :HierarchyName part goes right after the ___ name.
exercises.explain: For example "TM1SRV01:Region:Currency".

exercises.q: You have to type DBHW formulas by hand.
exercises.explain: Slice generates them automatically when exporting a view with hierarchies.

units.title: MDX Forms
units.objective: Drive a whole report from one MDX query, then make it dynamic with cells and dropdowns.

sources.title: What is an MDX Form and How Does it Work?
Building an MDX Form in Slice
Building a Dynamic MDX Form with Dimension Switching

lessons.title: What is an MDX Form?
lessons.tip: An MDX Form drives a whole report from one MDX query through a single MDXForm function.

exercises.q: What drives an MDX Form?
exercises.explain: One function, with an MDX query as its core parameter, renders the whole report.

exercises.q: MDX Forms were introduced in Slice v___.
exercises.explain: MDX Forms arrived in Slice v3.3.

exercises.q: Match each hidden component to its role
pairs: The statement that drives the report
Cell styles, always 7 rows x 2 columns
exercises.explain: These sit in hidden rows 1 to 10 of an exported MDX Form.

exercises.q: In an MDX Form, both rows and columns can expand and collapse.
exercises.explain: Classic Active Forms only expand and collapse rows.

exercises.q: Which works in MDX Forms but not in traditional Active Forms?
exercises.explain: Active Forms do rows and hierarchies, but not on-the-fly calculations.

lessons.title: Building an MDX Form
lessons.tip: Insert an MDX Form with a right-click in Excel, or export one from the Cube Viewer.

exercises.q: Insert an MDX Form from Excel
items: Go to Slice > Insert Form > MDX Form
Select the server, cube and view
exercises.explain: Slice inserts the MDXForm function and a format area.

exercises.q: Match each MDXForm argument to its purpose
pairs: The query that drives the report
exercises.explain: The other two arguments are Server and FormatRange.

exercises.q: With WriteBack set to 1, TM1 rules and security are bypassed.
exercises.explain: TM1 rules and security always take precedence.

exercises.q: After export, unhide rows 1 to ___ to see the MDX Form parts.
exercises.explain: Rows 1 to 10 hold the MDX query, format range and MDXForm function.

exercises.q: How big must the Format Range be?
exercises.explain: The Format Range is always exactly 7 rows by 2 columns.

lessons.title: Dynamic MDX Forms
lessons.tip: Make an MDX Form dynamic by building its MDX query from cells, dropdowns and named ranges.

exercises.q: How can a user switch hierarchies without editing formulas?
options: Pick from a dropdown used in the MDX query
exercises.explain: A data validation list feeds the hierarchy name into the query.

exercises.q: On-the-fly calculated members use the MDX ___ clause.
exercises.explain: WITH MEMBER defines the calculation inside the query.

exercises.q: On-the-fly calculated members change the TM1 model.
exercises.explain: They exist only in the report. The model is never modified.

exercises.q: Why build a long MDX query with CONCATENATE?
options: A plain string in a cell is limited to 255 characters
exercises.explain: CONCATENATE assembles the query in pieces.

exercises.q: Match each tool to its role
pairs: Names a cell so the query can use it
Picks the matching MDX query from a table
Tests a query before you use it
exercises.explain: Together they let one sheet switch between many report layouts.

units.title: Report Burster
units.objective: Turn one template into a personalised report for every cost centre, region or other element with the Report Burster.

sources.title: Using the Report Burster in Slice
Key Insights from Slice Report Burster: Bugs Fixed and Known Limitations

lessons.title: Why burst reports?
lessons.tip: Bursting turns one master template into a personalised report for each element, like each cost centre.

exercises.q: What does bursting do?
options: Makes a personalised copy of a template per element
exercises.explain: Each copy contains only that element's data.

exercises.q: Recipients need TM1 access to read their bursted report.
exercises.explain: They just get an Excel file, with no login or Planning Analytics licence needed.

exercises.q: What Slice does for each element
items: Updates the SUBNM or filter cell
Saves the result as a new file
exercises.explain: Slice repeats this loop for every element in the chosen dimension.

exercises.q: Bursting runs the template once for each element in a chosen ___.
exercises.explain: For example, once per cost centre.

exercises.q: Which is a typical bursting use case?
options: Sending each manager their own P&L
exercises.explain: Monthly cost centre packs are the classic example.

lessons.title: Running the Report Burster
lessons.tip: Pick a sheet, set the cell to update and the MDX set to loop over, then click Burst.

exercises.q: The Report Burster needs a Slice Business license.
exercises.explain: Report Burster is a Business edition feature.

exercises.q: Match each parameter to its meaning
pairs: Cell the burster updates for each element
Set of elements to loop over
Optional name shown instead of the ID
exercises.explain: Add parameters with the + button.

exercises.q: Which output formats can you pick?
exercises.explain: You can also choose a single file or one file per element.

exercises.q: To add a parameter, click the ___ button.
exercises.explain: Each parameter has an Address, an MDX expression and an optional Alias.

exercises.q: Which option keeps live formulas or leaves static values?
exercises.explain: Choose whether outputs keep live TM1 formulas or only values.

lessons.title: Burster tips and limits
lessons.tip: Excel is busy while bursting, and file names can be cell references so every output is unique.

exercises.q: You can keep working in Excel while a burst runs.
exercises.explain: Excel and Slice are frozen until the burst finishes.

exercises.q: How do you stop a burst that is in progress?
options: End the Excel process in Task Manager
exercises.explain: There is no cancel button.

exercises.q: Output file names can be ___, so each report gets a unique name.
exercises.explain: They are re-evaluated on every iteration, formulas included.

exercises.q: Elements can be looped over from how many TM1 servers?
exercises.explain: A report can use several servers, but the loop comes from a single server.

exercises.q: Which option can slow down bursting on large reports?
exercises.explain: Removing formulas processes cell by cell, which takes longer.

units.title: Building fast reports (best practices)
units.objective: Find what slows a report down and apply the best practices that make Slice reports refresh fast.

sources.title: Building Fast Excel Reports with Slice

lessons.title: Find the bottlenecks
lessons.tip: Before you optimise, measure: the Audit report and the Slice logs show where a report loses time.

exercises.q: Which Slice tool lists the cubes, the TM1 formulas and the best-practice violations of a report?
exercises.explain: Run it on the sheet or the whole workbook to see what to fix first.

exercises.q: Slice logs can be set to levels such as Debug, Info, Warn and Error.
exercises.explain: Turn the levels on or off as needed to track requests and find bottlenecks.

exercises.q: In the manual's case study, a report took 2-3 seconds on premise. How long did it take in PAfE on the cloud?
exercises.explain: Over the network every request counts, so report design matters more.

exercises.q: Match each Slice tool to what it helps you do
pairs: Lists cubes, TM1 formulas and violations
Keeps an audit trail of requests
Debugs a TM1 formula in Excel
exercises.explain: Use them together to find slow queries.

exercises.q: Use Slice's auditing tools to find slow queries ___ deploying changes.
exercises.explain: Test and fix a report before your users get it.

lessons.title: Build fast reports
lessons.tip: Fewer, batched requests mean faster reports: prefer DBRW and keep views symmetric.

exercises.q: Why replace DBR with DBRW?
options: DBRW requests can be grouped; DBR sends one per cell
exercises.explain: In one example, this cut refresh time from 6 seconds to 1.

exercises.q: Doing arithmetic inside a DBRW formula helps Slice batch requests.
exercises.explain: Arithmetic stops batching. Do the math in a separate cell.

exercises.q: TM1ELLIST can be a better alternative to many ___ formulas.
exercises.explain: Each SUBNM sends its own request to TM1.

exercises.q: Adding Budget in the middle of the columns makes the view...
exercises.explain: In the example, one query became three.

exercises.q: Match each item to its effect on speed
pairs: Grouped into a single MDX query
Lists cubes, TM1 formulas and violations
exercises.explain: Use the audit report to find and fix bottlenecks.

lessons.title: Batch your formulas
lessons.tip: Slice is fastest when DBRWs can be grouped into a single request: keep each one alone in its cell.

exercises.q: Each ___ formula sends a separate request to the server.
exercises.explain: Replacing DBRs with DBRWs lets Slice consolidate the requests.

exercises.q: Where should you do arithmetic on a DBRW result?
exercises.explain: Arithmetic inside a DB formula stops batching.

exercises.q: Why do several DBRWs nested in one cell slow a report down?
options: Their dependencies stop them being batched
exercises.explain: Design reports so DBRWs can be grouped into a single request.

exercises.q: SUBNM formulas in error are harmless and can be left in a report.
exercises.explain: Each SUBNM sends its own request: remove the ones that are invalid or not needed.

exercises.q: Match each item to its effect on refresh time
exercises.explain: Fewer, batched requests make a faster report.

units.title: Going live
units.objective: Move from Perspectives and get Slice ready for your users in production.

sources.title: Transitioning from TM1 Perspectives to Slice
Good practices before going live with Slice

lessons.title: Moving from Perspectives
lessons.tip: Perspectives reports work in Slice, though action buttons need converting and some clean-up helps.

exercises.q: You can install Perspectives and Slice, but only one should be enabled at a time.
exercises.explain: Switch by enabling or disabling the add-in and restarting Excel.

exercises.q: What must be converted for Perspectives reports to work in Slice?
exercises.explain: Slice's Convert Buttons tool does this for a workbook or a whole folder.

exercises.q: To convert buttons, Perspectives must be installed but ___.
exercises.explain: Slice needs the Perspectives libraries but can't run alongside Perspectives.

exercises.q: Match each item to its description
pairs: Connects directly to TM1, often needs Citrix
Uses the REST API from the user's laptop
Converts action buttons in a workbook or folder
exercises.explain: Slice is built for the WAN, so no Citrix is required.

exercises.q: Which Excel setting does button conversion need?
options: Trust access to the VBA project object model
exercises.explain: Enable VBA macros and trust access to the VBA project object model.

lessons.title: Ready for production
lessons.tip: Onboard your users, monitor workbooks with Pulse, and lock shared settings if needed.

exercises.q: One large, badly built workbook can impact all other users.
exercises.explain: That's why good practices matter before going live.

exercises.q: Why can Pulse monitor workbook activity with Slice?
options: Slice sends workbook and sheet names to the TM1 session
exercises.explain: Perspectives does not send this, Slice does.

exercises.q: Settings locked in ___ are greyed out in Slice > Settings.
exercises.explain: Available from Slice v6.1.

exercises.q: In desktop.overrides.yml, commented-out settings stay under the user's control.
exercises.explain: Only uncommented settings are locked.

exercises.q: Roll out locked settings to all users
items: Configure Slice in Slice > Settings on one PC
Restart Excel and check the greyed-out fields
Give both files to IT to deploy
exercises.explain: IT copies desktop.yml and desktop.overrides.yml into each user's %APPDATA%\ArcForTm1 folder.

courses.title: Arc
courses.description: Learn Arc, one short lesson a day.

units.title: Arc basics
units.objective: Open Arc, log in to a TM1 instance, store your credentials and find any object fast.

sources.title: Filtering the Search by Instance and Objects

lessons.title: Opening Arc
lessons.tip: Run the Arc executable, then open http://localhost:7070/ and pick a TM1 instance.

exercises.q: Which URL do you open after running the Arc executable?
exercises.explain: The manual says to run the executable and go to http://localhost:7070/.

exercises.q: Put the steps to access Arc in order
exercises.explain: Start Arc, open its URL, pick the instance, then log in.

exercises.q: In the training setup, you log in to TM1SRV01 with the user admin.
exercises.explain: Click TM1SRV01 and log in as admin with the password apple.

exercises.q: Which one is NOT one of Arc's three main sections?
exercises.explain: Arc is split into the Menu, the Workbench and the Top Bar.

exercises.q: Arc is split into the Menu, the Workbench and the Top ___.
exercises.explain: The three main sections are Menu, Workbench and Top Bar.

lessons.title: Storing credentials
lessons.tip: Arc can remember your TM1 credentials, set from the Settings tab of the About page.

exercises.q: Where do you turn on Store Credentials?
exercises.explain: Click the About / Info icon, go to Settings and tick Store Credentials under TM1 Credentials.

exercises.q: Arc can also store ODBC and Pulse credentials.
exercises.explain: TM1, ODBC and Pulse credentials can all be stored when the option is on.

exercises.q: What does Arc show when you enable this option?
exercises.explain: Storing credentials carries security risks, so Arc displays a warning.

exercises.q: Storing credentials is a good idea on a shared workstation.
exercises.explain: Only use it on machines you control, never on shared workstations or servers.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Log in to a TM1 instance
exercises.explain: Log in first, then About, Settings and the Store Credentials option.

lessons.title: Finding objects
lessons.tip: Use i: and t: in the search box to filter by instance and object type.

exercises.q: Type budget ___ to find processes with budget in the name.
exercises.explain: t:p (or t:process) filters the results to processes.

exercises.q: Match each filter to what it shows
exercises.explain: t: filters by object type: p, d, cube and cho.

exercises.q: What does i:cxmd do?
options: Shows only objects from the cxmd instance
exercises.explain: i: filters the results by TM1 instance.

exercises.q: You can combine filters, like i:cxmd t:process.
exercises.explain: Combined filters show only processes in the cxmd instance.

exercises.q: You must press Enter to see the search results.
exercises.explain: Results update immediately as you type.

units.title: Process Editor
units.objective: Know the parts of a TI process in Arc and keep your work safe with auto-save.

lessons.title: The Process Editor
lessons.tip: A TI process has four code tabs: Prolog, Metadata, Data and Epilog.

exercises.q: Which phase runs once, before the data loop?
exercises.explain: Prolog runs once before the data loop, for setup such as clearing data.

exercises.q: Put the process phases in the order they run
exercises.explain: Prolog first, then Metadata and Data per record, then Epilog.

exercises.q: Match each phase to its typical use
exercises.explain: Keep setup in Prolog, cube writes in Data and teardown in Epilog.

exercises.q: Arc flags TI syntax errors inline before you save or run.
exercises.explain: Arc validates TI code in real time, which reduces failed runs.

exercises.q: Which tab defines inputs passed to the process at runtime?
exercises.explain: Parameters can be passed by chores, other processes or user prompts.

lessons.title: Auto-save
lessons.tip: From Arc v3.4, Arc can save your TI processes to TM1 at a set interval.

exercises.q: Where do you enable Auto-Save Processes?
exercises.explain: Open About, go to Settings, click Processes and tick Auto-Save Processes.

exercises.q: Auto-save is on by default.
exercises.explain: It is off by default; you switch it on in the settings.

exercises.q: Auto-save saves directly to the TM1 ___.
exercises.explain: Each save goes to the TM1 server, not just locally in the browser.

exercises.q: TM1 rejects an auto-save of a process with syntax errors.
exercises.explain: Auto-save still tries, but TM1 rejects saves with errors.

exercises.q: When is auto-save especially useful?
options: On a cloud TM1 with patchy internet
exercises.explain: It protects your work from browser disconnections or internet issues.

units.title: Debugging
units.objective: Step through a TI process, use conditional breakpoints and the debugging shortcuts.

lessons.title: Debugging basics
lessons.tip: Debugging lets you step through a TI process line by line and watch the variable values.

exercises.q: Which tm1s.cfg setting must be true to debug TI?
exercises.explain: Debugging needs EnableTIDebugging=true in tm1s.cfg.

exercises.q: Which action does not enter a child process called by ExecuteProcess?
exercises.explain: Step Over moves line by line but does not enter child processes.

exercises.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Runs to the end or next breakpoint
exercises.explain: These are the key debugging terms in Arc.

exercises.q: With debugging, you no longer need to write values out to ASCII files.
exercises.explain: You can see the variable values change in real time instead.

exercises.q: Use Step ___ with Step In to leave a child process.
exercises.explain: Step Out runs to the end of the child process and stops in the caller.

lessons.title: Conditional breakpoints
lessons.tip: Add a condition to a breakpoint so it only stops when the expression is true.

exercises.q: The condition vEmployee @= '998320692' stops only for that employee.
exercises.explain: The breakpoint stops only when its expression is true.

exercises.q: Where do you type the condition?
exercises.explain: Add the condition in the Breakpoints tab, then save.

exercises.q: In the example, which tab gets the breakpoint?
exercises.explain: The breakpoint is added in the Data tab, which runs per employee.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Add a breakpoint in the Data tab
Type the condition in the Breakpoints tab
exercises.explain: Set the breakpoint, add the condition, save, then Continue.

exercises.q: Without a condition, the breakpoint stops for every ___.
exercises.explain: A condition avoids stopping on every employee record.

lessons.title: Shortcut keys
lessons.tip: Use F8, F10 and F11 to debug, and CTRL shortcuts to work faster in the editor.

exercises.q: Press ___ to Continue while debugging.
exercises.explain: F8 is Continue, F10 is Step Over and F11 is Step In.

exercises.q: Match each key to its debugging action
exercises.explain: These are the Windows debugging shortcuts.

exercises.q: Which shortcut executes the process on Windows?
exercises.explain: CTRL+SHIFT+E executes; CTRL+ENTER enters full screen.

exercises.q: What does CTRL+M do?
exercises.explain: CTRL+M hides or shows the menu, and ALT+M goes to search.

exercises.q: CTRL+H opens Find on Windows.
exercises.explain: CTRL+F is Find; CTRL+H is Replace.

units.title: Cube Viewer
units.objective: Arrange, save and export cube views, and enter data straight into TM1.

sources.title: Cube Viewer – Data Entry and Spreading

lessons.title: Navigating views
lessons.tip: The Cube Viewer works like a pivot table: drag dimensions between title, rows and columns.

exercises.q: Match each area to what it does
exercises.explain: Drag a dimension pill to the area you want.

exercises.q: Which export format gives values only, with no TM1 formulas?
exercises.explain: Snapshot exports values only; Slice and Active Form keep TM1 formulas.

exercises.q: A Native View supports hierarchies.
exercises.explain: MDX Views support hierarchies; Native Views do not.

exercises.q: Who can save a public view?
exercises.explain: Unticking Private makes a public view, which only administrators can set.

exercises.q: You can stack several dimensions in the row area.
exercises.explain: Stacking dimensions in rows or columns adds depth to the data.

lessons.title: Entering data
lessons.tip: Type into white cells; consolidations recalculate on their own.

exercises.q: You can type values into consolidated cells.
exercises.explain: Only white cells are writable; consolidations are calculated.

exercises.q: How do you copy a value across a row?
exercises.explain: Hover the bottom-right corner, then hold and drag to the right.

exercises.q: Where do you find TM1 data spreading?
exercises.explain: Right-click a data cell and pick a spreading method.

exercises.q: Click ___ Data Entry to revert your edits.
exercises.explain: Undo Data Entry reverts the cells to their values before your edits.

exercises.q: If consolidations don't update, click Refresh Values.
exercises.explain: Consolidations usually recalculate, and Refresh Values forces it.

units.title: Subsets and dimensions
units.objective: Filter and organise elements in the Subset Editor and set default members.

sources.title: Subset Editor – Filtering and Organising Elements
Set a Default Member for Your Dimensions

lessons.title: Subset Editor
lessons.tip: The Subset Editor filters and orders elements without changing the dimension.

exercises.q: Filter by Level ___ to keep only leaf elements.
exercises.explain: Level 0 returns only leaf elements, without consolidations.

exercises.q: Filtering a subset changes the underlying dimension.
exercises.explain: You filter and reorder elements without modifying the dimension.

exercises.q: Which button shows the MDX behind your filters?
exercises.explain: Show MDX displays the expression that defines the current subset.

exercises.q: Put the steps to keep some elements in order
exercises.explain: Filter, select several with CTRL, then click Keep.

exercises.q: Search results appear as you type, with no need to press Enter.
exercises.explain: Matching elements are returned as you type in the Find box.

lessons.title: Default members
lessons.tip: In MDX views, dimensions not on rows or columns use their default member.

exercises.q: How does Arc mark the default member?
exercises.explain: In Arc, a * next to the element name in the pill shows the default member.

exercises.q: With no default member set, which element does TM1 use?
exercises.explain: TM1 uses the top consolidation, or the first element if there is none.

exercises.q: After editing }HierarchyProperties, run ___.
exercises.explain: RefreshMdxHierarchy picks up the new default member without a restart.

exercises.q: In Arc, Set as Default Member takes just one click.
exercises.explain: Pick the element in the pill and click Set as Default Member.

exercises.q: Changing defaultMember requires a TM1 server restart.
exercises.explain: RefreshMdxHierarchy applies it without restarting the server.

units.title: Productivity
units.objective: Test MDX in the MDX Lab and add your own code snippets to auto-complete.

lessons.title: MDX Lab
lessons.tip: MDX Lab lets you write, run and format MDX queries, with CTRL+SPACE autocomplete.

exercises.q: In MDX Lab, press ___ to open autocomplete.
exercises.explain: CTRL+SPACE opens the autocomplete panel for MDX functions and snippets.

exercises.q: Where do you open MDX Lab?
exercises.explain: Expand Tools in the left menu and click MDX Lab.

exercises.q: Highlighting part of a query and clicking Execute runs only that part.
exercises.explain: Only the selected text is sent to the server.

exercises.q: What does the JSON toggle show?
exercises.explain: Tick JSON in the Result header to see the raw TM1 REST API payload.

exercises.q: Match each MDX pattern to what it does
exercises.explain: These are common MDX patterns you can test in MDX Lab.

lessons.title: Your own snippets
lessons.tip: Create .hjson files in Arc/snippets to add your own auto-complete entries.

exercises.q: In which file format do you create your own snippets?
exercises.explain: Custom snippets are .hjson files in the Arc/snippets folder.

exercises.q: You must restart Arc to see new snippets.
exercises.explain: Just save the file and refresh the browser (SHIFT+F5).

exercises.q: In a snippet, ___ is what you see in the auto-complete list.
exercises.explain: value is the label in the list; snippet is the code inserted.

exercises.q: Why start a snippet's value with @?
exercises.explain: Type @my to filter the list to your own snippets.

exercises.q: Placeholders with the same number stay in sync.
exercises.explain: All ${1:sDim} placeholders update together when you tab to them.

units.title: Security and sessions
units.objective: Manage TM1 users and groups in the Security Editor and control session timeouts.

sources.title: Deep Dive into the Arc TM1 Security Editor

lessons.title: Security Editor
lessons.tip: The Security Editor under Administration manages TM1 users, groups and access in one place.

exercises.q: Where is the Security Editor?
exercises.explain: Go to Administration > Security, then pick your TM1 instance.

exercises.q: Match each button to what it does
pairs: Shows all access for a user
Lists the users in a group
exercises.explain: These buttons speed up tasks that take several steps in Architect.

exercises.q: Impersonate is available to TM1 Administrators only.
exercises.explain: Impersonation is restricted to TM1 Administrators.

exercises.q: Changes made while impersonating apply to your own account.
exercises.explain: They apply to the impersonated user's account, so use it with care.

exercises.q: What does the Audit tab summarise?
exercises.explain: It counts admins and lists users without groups and groups without users.

lessons.title: Session timeouts
lessons.tip: Arc has two timeouts: the TM1 REST session in tm1s.cfg and the Arc session in settings.yml.

exercises.q: Which parameter sets the TM1 REST session timeout?
exercises.explain: HTTPSessionTimeoutMinutes is set per TM1 server in tm1s.cfg.

exercises.q: Changing HTTPSessionTimeoutMinutes needs a TM1 restart.
exercises.explain: The parameter is dynamic and takes effect without a restart.

exercises.q: The Arc session timeout is set in ___.
exercises.explain: sessiontimeout in settings.yml controls the Arc browser session.

exercises.q: What is the default TM1 session timeout?
exercises.explain: HTTPSessionTimeoutMinutes defaults to 20 minutes.

exercises.q: After changing sessiontimeout, you restart Arc.
exercises.explain: Changes to settings.yml need an Arc restart.

units.title: Plugins
units.objective: Install plugins with the Plugins Manager and control who can manage them.

sources.title: How to Install Plugins with the Plugins Manager

lessons.title: Plugins Manager
lessons.tip: Tools > Plugins Manager installs Cubewise plugins once for every user of your Arc.

exercises.q: Where do you open the Plugins Manager?
exercises.explain: The Plugins Manager is under Tools in the left menu.

exercises.q: An installed plugin appears for every user after they reload.
exercises.explain: A plugin is installed once for the whole Arc server.

exercises.q: Match each status to its meaning
exercises.explain: The status tells you what Install would do.

exercises.q: Put the install steps in order
exercises.explain: Reload Arc so the browser loads the new set of plugins.

exercises.q: What does the Arc server need to load the catalogue?
exercises.explain: Without access to GitHub, the page cannot load the plugin catalogue.

lessons.title: Arc permissions
lessons.tip: The arcpermissions block in settings.yml decides who can install and remove plugins.

exercises.q: With no arcpermissions block, any user can install plugins.
exercises.explain: Without the block every capability check denies, so installing is disabled.

exercises.q: Which capability allows installing and updating plugins?
exercises.explain: plugins.install covers installing and updating; plugins.remove covers removing.

exercises.q: A rule with no grants gives full ___ rights.
exercises.explain: A rule without grants gives *, which is everything.

exercises.q: What does an invalid arcpermissions block grant?
exercises.explain: A block Arc can't understand is invalid and grants nothing.

exercises.q: What-if lets you try a block without changing settings.yml.
exercises.explain: Click What-if, try a block, then Back to live to return.

courses.title: Pulse
courses.description: Learn Pulse, one short lesson a day.

units.title: Pulse basics
units.objective: Understand what Pulse is, how it runs and where to see all your TM1 instances at a glance.

sources.title: Monitor and Manage Your TM1 Environment in One Place

lessons.title: What is Pulse?
lessons.tip: Pulse brings monitoring, migration, documentation, change tracking and analytics for TM1 into one application.

exercises.q: Who is Pulse mainly designed for?
exercises.explain: Pulse is a management platform designed for IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) administrators.

exercises.q: Pulse runs as two ___ that track your TM1 instances.
exercises.explain: Pulse runs as two services that track your TM1 instances and update two internal databases.

exercises.q: Pulse must be installed on each server where TM1 is running.
exercises.explain: Pulse needs to run on every server that hosts TM1.

exercises.q: Match each Pulse feature to what it does
pairs: Shows CPU, memory and sessions live
Keeps a Git history of TM1 objects
Tracks who uses TM1 and how
exercises.explain: These are some of the key features Pulse brings together in one place.

exercises.q: What does the light Pulse Excel add-in monitor?
exercises.explain: The add-in reports each time a user creates, saves, opens or closes a workbook with TM1 formulas.

lessons.title: Overview and Dashboard
lessons.tip: The Overview is the Pulse homepage, and the Dashboard summarises one environment.

exercises.q: Clicking an environment on the Overview page opens its Dashboard.
exercises.explain: On the Overview page, click one environment to open the Dashboard.

exercises.q: What opens when you click an instance on the Overview page?
exercises.explain: Clicking an instance opens the Pulse Live Monitoring feature.

exercises.q: The # column in Instance State is the ___ shown in Task Manager.
exercises.explain: The "#" is the process identifier (PID) in Task Manager.

exercises.q: Put the Dashboard sections in order, top to bottom
exercises.explain: The Dashboard runs from the KPI panel down to the server information.

exercises.q: Server Information is shown when you use Planning Analytics Cloud.
exercises.explain: OS, memory, CPU and disk details are not available on Planning Analytics Cloud.

units.title: Live monitoring
units.objective: Watch a TM1 instance in real time and find out who is waiting or making others wait.

lessons.title: The Live Monitor
lessons.tip: The Live Monitor shows the KPIs, sessions and message log of one TM1 instance.

exercises.q: Which button shows only sessions that are running something?
exercises.explain: Hide Idle filters the session list down to the active sessions.

exercises.q: Match each Live Monitor section to what it shows
pairs: CPU, memory, users and wait time
exercises.explain: The Live Monitor has three parts: the KPIs, the sessions and the message log.

exercises.q: You can restart the instance from the Live Monitor with Service Control.
exercises.explain: Click Service Control in the Monitor to restart the instance.

exercises.q: Which action is in the last column of the session list?
exercises.explain: The last column lets you see session details, cancel a thread or disconnect the session.

exercises.q: You can filter the message log to show only ___ entries.
exercises.explain: Pulse lets you filter the message log by type, for example only ERROR.

lessons.title: User sessions
lessons.tip: User Sessions is the first place to check when users say TM1 is slow.

exercises.q: Where do you find User Sessions?
exercises.explain: User Sessions is under Reports > User Analytics.

exercises.q: Which column shows users whose operations make others wait?
exercises.explain: Others Waiting % identifies the users causing locks that affect the rest of the system.

exercises.q: Waiting % is the share of a user's time spent in a wait state.
exercises.explain: Waiting % is the percentage of the user's time spent locked by another thread.

exercises.q: Click a user's name to see the Long Running ___ chart.
exercises.explain: The Long Running Operations chart pinpoints which action was slow.

exercises.q: Put the investigation steps in order
exercises.explain: Start from the sessions table, then drill into one user and their operations.

units.title: Alerts
units.objective: Set up proactive alerts so you hear about TM1 problems before your users do.

lessons.title: Alert types
lessons.tip: Alerts are created in Administration > Alerts, and each type watches one kind of problem.

exercises.q: Which alert fires when a TM1 instance cannot be contacted?
exercises.explain: Offline triggers when an instance is not started, has been stopped or has crashed.

exercises.q: Match each alert type to its trigger
pairs: Too many users in a wait state
Free disk space drops too low
exercises.explain: Each alert type watches a different symptom.

exercises.q: Leave the instance blank on a Memory alert to apply it at server level.
exercises.explain: A blank instance field applies Memory and CPU alerts to the whole server.

exercises.q: Process Run Time compares a run with its historical ___.
exercises.explain: It triggers when a process runs longer than its historical average by the set percentage.

exercises.q: Which alert watches the tm1server.log file?
exercises.explain: Message In Log triggers when text in tm1server.log matches a wildcard pattern.

lessons.title: Recommended alerts
lessons.tip: Cubewise recommends a small set of alerts for every production server.

exercises.q: What Memory threshold is recommended for production?
exercises.explain: The recommended Memory alert is 80%, repeating every 20 minutes.

exercises.q: What is the recommended Disk Free Space threshold?
exercises.explain: The recommended Disk Free Space alert is 10GB, repeating every 60 minutes.

exercises.q: For the recommended alerts, the Instance field should be left blank.
exercises.explain: Each recommended alert is set with a blank Instance.

exercises.q: The recommended Cancel Thread alert filters on ___.
exercises.explain: Cancel Thread is set to 600 seconds with a ViewArrayConstruct filter.

exercises.q: Match each recommended alert to its setting
exercises.explain: These are the recommended thresholds for production servers.

lessons.title: Alert templates
lessons.tip: Alert templates save default settings so you can create alerts in a few clicks.

exercises.q: What is an alert template?
options: A saved alert configuration with defaults
exercises.explain: A template stores default settings such as type, thresholds and notification group.

exercises.q: To create alerts from templates, click ___ on the Alerts page.
exercises.explain: Generate from Templates creates alerts for an instance in one go.

exercises.q: In which format are alert templates exported?
exercises.explain: Export downloads a JSON file you can import on another Pulse server.

exercises.q: Reset Default reverts alert types and templates to their out-of-the-box values.
exercises.explain: Reset Default restores the original alert types and templates.

exercises.q: Put the steps to generate alerts in order
exercises.explain: Pick templates and a group, then the target instance, then finish.

units.title: Change tracking
units.objective: Know who changed which TM1 object and when, and roll back a bad change without downtime.

sources.title: Enabling Change Tracking and Source Control
Viewing TM1 Object History and Using Rollback

lessons.title: Tracking changes
lessons.tip: Pulse logs every change to a TM1 object and keeps each version in Git.

exercises.q: Pulse change tracking records data changes inside cubes.
exercises.explain: Pulse tracks objects such as cubes, dimensions, processes and chores, not cube data.

exercises.q: Pulse uses ___ to store every change to your TM1 objects.
exercises.explain: Pulse source control is built on Git.

exercises.q: Match each setting or feature to its role
pairs: Stores each version to retrieve later
Admin account Pulse uses for TM1
exercises.explain: Change tracking and source control work together, using an admin account to read TM1.

exercises.q: How long are changes kept in Pulse source control?
exercises.explain: Changes are stored forever, so you can always get old versions back.

exercises.q: Put the steps to enable change tracking in order
exercises.explain: Set it in Instance Settings, then repeat for each TM1 instance.

lessons.title: History and rollback
lessons.tip: You can restore any TM1 object to an earlier version while TM1 keeps running.

exercises.q: Rolling back a TM1 object requires a restart of TM1.
exercises.explain: Rollback is applied live, with no TM1 downtime.

exercises.q: In the diff view, what does green mean?
exercises.explain: Red shows removed lines and green shows added lines.

exercises.q: Click ___ to see an object's full change history.
exercises.explain: History shows every change since tracking began.

exercises.q: How long is the change history kept?
options: Since tracking began, with no expiry
exercises.explain: The full history is kept from when change tracking was first enabled.

exercises.q: Put the rollback steps in order
items: Go to Change Tracking and pick an instance
Click Rollback next to a version
exercises.explain: Find the object, open its history, then roll back to the version you want.

units.title: Migration
units.objective: Package TM1 changes with their dependencies and promote them live or offline.

lessons.title: Migration packages
lessons.tip: A migration package holds the objects to move, and Pulse adds their dependencies for you.

exercises.q: Put the migration steps in order
exercises.explain: Create the package, move it between Pulse servers if needed, then execute it.

exercises.q: Download and Import are not needed when one Pulse server monitors both instances.
exercises.explain: Those steps are only needed when the target is on a separate Pulse server.

exercises.q: Which package method lets you query changes by date and developer?
exercises.explain: Source Control lists changes for a date range and optional user.

exercises.q: What is another name for an Offline Update package?
exercises.explain: Offline Update (Cold Promote) holds native TM1 files to copy while TM1 is stopped.

exercises.q: Migrating a dimension adds the .dimd and ___ files.
exercises.explain: A dimension uses .dimd and .dimx files, while .cubx holds cube information.

lessons.title: Executing a package
lessons.tip: Pulse applies only the incremental changes to a running TM1 instance.

exercises.q: The target TM1 instance must be running to execute the package.
exercises.explain: Pulse applies changes through TI functions and API calls while TM1 is up.

exercises.q: What is the default Line Change Sensitivity for rules?
exercises.explain: Changes within 5 lines of each other are combined; use 1 to separate all changes.

exercises.q: What does Backup Data Directory run first?
exercises.explain: It runs Save Data All, then zips the whole data directory.

exercises.q: Match each execution option to what it does
pairs: Runs a Security Refresh at the end
Only adds dependencies that do not exist
exercises.explain: These options make a migration safer on the target instance.

exercises.q: For processes with an ___ data source, you enter credentials before executing.
exercises.explain: Processes with ODBC credentials need a user name and password on the Execution page.

lessons.title: Offline migration
lessons.tip: An offline package is copied into the data directory while TM1 is stopped.

exercises.q: Which folders does an offline package contain?
exercises.explain: items holds the selected objects and dependencies holds related objects.

exercises.q: Offline migration works on any TM1 instance, including IBM cloud.
exercises.explain: Offline migration is only for instances on-premise or on a private cloud.

exercises.q: Skip dependency files that already ___ in the target.
exercises.explain: Copy items over existing files, but copy dependencies only if they are missing.

exercises.q: Put the offline steps in order
exercises.explain: Save, stop, copy the files, then start TM1 again.

exercises.q: Which option creates an offline package when you save it?
exercises.explain: Select Offline Update (or Both) when saving the package.

units.title: Documentation
units.objective: Use the documentation Pulse builds automatically to understand and explain your TM1 model.

lessons.title: Model documentation
lessons.tip: Pulse documents your TM1 model automatically, so it is always up to date.

exercises.q: Match each report to what it shows
pairs: Which dimension is in which cube
exercises.explain: Pulse produces several reports from the same documentation data.

exercises.q: If documentation fails, many other Pulse features will not work.
exercises.explain: The documentation is the backbone of Pulse.

exercises.q: Which list shows a process's data source type and last run time?
exercises.explain: The Process List shows data source type, query and last run time.

exercises.q: The ___ report checks naming conventions and code in rules and processes.
exercises.explain: The Validation report checks the model against the best practices you define.

exercises.q: Which list shows if a chore is Active and its Start Time?
exercises.explain: The Chore List shows Active, Start Time and Last run.

lessons.title: Model Spotlight
lessons.tip: Model Spotlight gives an overview of one TM1 application and each of its objects.

exercises.q: In cube statistics, what may point to overfeeding?
options: Numbers is higher than Cells Fed
Cells Fed is more than twice Numbers
exercises.explain: If Cells Fed is more than twice Numbers, there might be an overfeeding issue.

exercises.q: Over how many days does Model Spotlight show changes by author?
exercises.explain: It shows the number of changes by author and day for the past 14 days.

exercises.q: A cube's Description appears in the cube list and the technical documentation.
exercises.explain: That is why it is worth filling in the Description field.

exercises.q: In Performance Statistics, ___ is the number of numeric cells.
exercises.explain: Numbers counts numeric cells and Cells Fed counts fed cells.

exercises.q: When does Pulse store cube statistics?
exercises.explain: Stored statistics let you see when a metric such as feeders increased.

units.title: Explorer and reports
units.objective: Dig into past TM1 activity with the Pulse Explorer and schedule a health report.

lessons.title: The Pulse Explorer
lessons.tip: Pulse stores everything that happens on your TM1 instances so you can explore it later.

exercises.q: The Pulse Explorer is powered by Opensearch Dashboards.
exercises.explain: Pulse stores activity in an embedded Opensearch cluster and the Explorer reads it.

exercises.q: Which Pulse version introduced the Explorer?
exercises.explain: The Pulse Explorer was introduced with Pulse v6.

exercises.q: Set ___ to match the disk space available for Pulse data.
exercises.explain: More data means more history, so size MaximumPulseDiskSpaceGB to your disk.

exercises.q: Who can see the Explorer link under Overview?
exercises.explain: The Explorer button is only available for Pulse Admins.

exercises.q: What period does a dashboard show by default?
exercises.explain: By default the date picker shows the last 15 minutes.

lessons.title: System Summary Report
lessons.tip: The System Summary Report is a scheduled health check emailed to your team.

exercises.q: Put the report's three parts in order
exercises.explain: The report starts with activity and incidents, then waits, then alerts by type.

exercises.q: Where do you open the System Summary Report?
exercises.explain: It is under Reports > Performance > System Summary.

exercises.q: Only Pulse admins can run it, but any notification group can receive it.
exercises.explain: The report is admin only but can be emailed to any notification group.

exercises.q: Match the days selected to the breakdown
exercises.explain: The period breakdown adapts to the number of days selected.

exercises.q: Wait Time Analysis lists the top ___ waiting events.
exercises.explain: It shows the top 10 waiting events and the maximum wait time by period.

units.title: Users and licences
units.objective: See who uses your TM1 Excel reports and right-size your IBM licences.

lessons.title: Excel workbooks
lessons.tip: Pulse Excel Logging shows which TM1-connected workbooks are used, by whom and how often.

exercises.q: Where do you see the TM1 workbooks users opened?
exercises.explain: Reports > Excel Workbooks lists each workbook, who opened it and how often.

exercises.q: Clicking a workbook shows stats broken down by sheet.
exercises.explain: Drill into a workbook to see which sheets are used and how actively.

exercises.q: Excel Logging tracks workbooks that contain TM1 ___.
exercises.explain: Only workbooks containing TM1 formulas are tracked.

exercises.q: Which question does Excel Logging help answer?
options: Which reports are used or abandoned
exercises.explain: It shows which reports are actively used, helping with maintenance and training.

exercises.q: Match each view to what it shows
pairs: Fixes when no data is captured
exercises.explain: Start from the list, drill into a workbook, and troubleshoot if nothing is logged.

lessons.title: License optimization
lessons.tip: The License Optimization Report shows how each TM1 licence is really used.

exercises.q: Which roles does Pulse use to classify TM1 users?
exercises.explain: Pulse classifies users as Read, Write or Administrator in line with TM1 security.

exercises.q: Since Pulse v7.0, the license report is built from Pulse's OpenSearch data.
exercises.explain: Pulse v7.0 rebuilt the old thick client report on the OpenSearch DB.

exercises.q: The license report exports to CSV or to ___ for audits.
exercises.explain: You can export to CSV and produce audit-ready reports in PDF.

exercises.q: Which is a benefit of license optimization?
exercises.explain: It helps you stay compliant during internal or external license audits.

exercises.q: A license report helps find inactive or dormant users.
exercises.explain: Finding dormant users is a key way to cut unused licences.

courses.title: PowerConnect
courses.description: Learn PowerConnect, one short lesson a day.

units.title: PowerConnect basics
units.objective: Understand what PowerConnect synchronises between TM1 and Power BI, and when to choose it over Atmosphere.

sources.title: PowerConnect vs Atmosphere: Choosing the Right Path for TM1 Data

lessons.title: What is PowerConnect?
lessons.tip: PowerConnect links IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) with Microsoft Power BI.

exercises.q: Which three things does PowerConnect synchronise?
exercises.explain: PowerConnect is built on three pillars: data, metadata and security.

exercises.q: PowerConnect only works with on-premises TM1.
exercises.explain: It supports on-premises, Planning Analytics on Cloud and hybrid setups, including multi-instance.

exercises.q: The PowerConnect Custom Connector is backed by the PowerConnect ___.
exercises.explain: The Cubewise REST-API-enabled Power BI connector is backed by the PowerConnect Service.

exercises.q: Match each pillar to what it brings
pairs: Cube values with ad-hoc and scheduled refreshes
exercises.explain: Data, metadata and security each stay in step with TM1.

exercises.q: Where can users see TM1 data through PowerConnect?
exercises.explain: PowerConnect works with Power BI Desktop, the Power BI Service and the Power BI mobile app.

lessons.title: PowerConnect or Atmosphere?
lessons.tip: Choose PowerConnect when Power BI is the destination, and Atmosphere when TM1 data must land in a database such as Snowflake.

exercises.q: PowerConnect moves data both ways, TM1 to Power BI and back.
exercises.explain: PowerConnect is one-way, TM1 to Power BI; two-way movement is an Atmosphere capability.

exercises.q: Where does PowerConnect data land?
exercises.explain: With PowerConnect the data lands inside the Power BI dataset.

exercises.q: Match each name to what it is
pairs: Direct connector from TM1 to Power BI
exercises.explain: The two products answer two different requirements.

exercises.q: With PowerConnect, which mindset do you work in?
exercises.explain: You shape data with views and subsets and lean on your existing TM1 security.

exercises.q: PowerConnect and Atmosphere can be used together.
exercises.explain: They are complementary: PowerConnect for Power BI reporting, Atmosphere for a shared data platform.

units.title: Getting started
units.objective: Connect PowerConnect to a TM1 instance and open the PowerConnect connector in Power BI Desktop.

lessons.title: Set up the training
lessons.tip: The training needs PowerConnect running, the hands-on TM1 instance and a connection in settings.yml.

exercises.q: Add the TM1 connection to the environments section of ___.
exercises.explain: Connection details go in the environments section of settings.yml.

exercises.q: settings.yml is in the conf folder of the PowerConnect installation.
exercises.explain: The file is under the conf folder of the PowerConnect installation directory.

exercises.q: Put the setup steps in order
items: Set up the hands-on TM1 instance
Enter the admin password in the portal
exercises.explain: Set up TM1, add the connection, restart the service, then log in to the configuration portal.

exercises.q: What do you do after editing settings.yml?
exercises.explain: Restart the PowerConnect service so it picks up the new connection.

exercises.q: Where is the configuration portal?
exercises.explain: The configuration portal is reachable at http://localhost/admin/.

lessons.title: Open the connector
lessons.tip: In Power BI Desktop, use Get Data to find the PowerConnect connector and point it at the PowerConnect URL.

exercises.q: What is the default PowerConnect Application URL?
exercises.explain: The connector asks for the PowerConnect Application URL, http://localhost:6060 by default.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Filter by ibm and pick the connector
exercises.explain: Find the connector through Get Data, then give it the PowerConnect URL.

exercises.q: Filter the connector list by "___" to find PowerConnect.
exercises.explain: Filter by ibm to see PowerConnect for IBM Planning Analytics/TM1.

exercises.q: The Navigator shows the TM1 connection name set up in the settings file.
exercises.explain: You see the connection name, such as TM1SERV01, and can expand its tree of TM1 objects.

exercises.q: Which Power BI Desktop tab holds Get Data?
exercises.explain: In the Home tab, click Get Data and search for the Cubewise connector.

units.title: Loading data
units.objective: Load TM1 data, subsets, attributes and security into Power BI Desktop.

sources.title: Loading Data and Metadata into Power BI

lessons.title: Data and metadata
lessons.tip: PowerConnect loads TM1 data from views or MDX, and metadata from subsets and attributes.

exercises.q: Besides a cube view, what can be a data source?
exercises.explain: TM1 data comes from an existing cube view or from your own MDX query.

exercises.q: Match each source to what it loads
exercises.explain: Views and MDX bring data; subsets and attributes bring metadata.

exercises.q: Data without metadata gives a flat table of numbers with cryptic codes.
exercises.explain: Metadata adds the labels and structure that make the numbers meaningful.

exercises.q: Element ___ such as descriptions and aliases come across with the data.
exercises.explain: Attributes let Power BI users see meaningful labels and filter by attribute values.

exercises.q: What does loading metadata let Power BI do?
options: Drill hierarchies and filter by attributes
exercises.explain: Metadata gives hierarchies to drill, descriptions for tooltips and attributes to filter.

lessons.title: Retrieving data
lessons.tip: Pick views, subsets and security in the Navigator, then check data types and table names before joining.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Open Get Data in Power BI Desktop
Search for Cubewise and click Connect
Check data types and table names
exercises.explain: Connect, pick what you need in the Navigator, then prepare the tables.

exercises.q: Selecting a subset also loads all attributes of its elements.
exercises.explain: When you select a subset in a hierarchy, all element attributes are loaded too.

exercises.q: Where do you pick the security to include?
exercises.explain: Select the dimensions with element level security in the Security node of the Navigator.

exercises.q: Why check the data types of element columns?
options: Power BI may read years as numbers
exercises.explain: When years are numeric, Power BI may treat the column as a number rather than text.

exercises.q: The Navigator shows a ___ of the data before it loads.
exercises.explain: The Navigator previews the data that will be loaded into Power BI.

units.title: Building a dashboard
units.objective: Prepare the loaded tables and build slicers and charts on TM1 data in Power BI Desktop.

lessons.title: Table View
lessons.tip: The Table View shows the raw data in each table and lets you fix data types.

exercises.q: What does the Σ symbol next to a column mean?
exercises.explain: Σ shows that Power BI has defined the column as a number.

exercises.q: Power BI automatically defined Year in GL_Data as a number.
exercises.explain: Both Amount and Year were automatically defined as numbers.

exercises.q: Change the Year column's data type to ___.
exercises.explain: Select Year in GL_Data and change its data type to Text.

exercises.q: What can you create and manage in the Table View?
exercises.explain: The Table View lets you work with calculated columns and measures.

exercises.q: After switching Year to Text, the Σ symbol stays.
exercises.explain: The Σ symbol next to Year disappears once it is Text.

lessons.title: Slicers
lessons.tip: Build slicers in the Report View, with a Year_Hierarchy so all periods consolidate.

exercises.q: What is the Report View for?
exercises.explain: The Report View is the drag-and-drop place to design interactive visuals and dashboards.

exercises.q: From level000 of Period, create a hierarchy named ___.
exercises.explain: Create Year_Hierarchy from level000 in the Model View.

exercises.q: The Year slicer uses Year from GL_Data because no Year subset was loaded.
exercises.explain: No subset of the year dimension was loaded, so Year comes from GL_Data.

exercises.q: Why create Year_Hierarchy?
options: So periods consolidate when Year or All is picked
exercises.explain: It makes all periods consolidate when Year or All is selected in the Slicer.

exercises.q: Match each item to its role
exercises.explain: Build in the Report View, create hierarchies in the Model View.

lessons.title: Charts
lessons.tip: Combine Amount from GL_Data with descriptions from the metadata tables to build charts.

exercises.q: Which visual lists expense accounts from highest to lowest?
exercises.explain: A multi-row card shows all expense accounts sorted by value.

exercises.q: Match each chart to what it shows
exercises.explain: Each chart combines Amount from GL_Data with a Description from metadata.

exercises.q: In the pie chart, Description comes from the Expenses metadata.
exercises.explain: Description comes from the Expenses metadata and Amount from GL_Data.

exercises.q: Numbers hard to read? Format the ___ column in the Table View.
exercises.explain: Select GL_Data in the Table View and format the Amount column.

exercises.q: In the treemap, where does Description come from?
exercises.explain: The treemap uses Description from the Department metadata.

units.title: TM1 hierarchies
units.objective: Make TM1 hierarchies roll up correctly in Power BI, without double counting or blank rows.

sources.title: Working with TM1 Hierarchies in Power BI

lessons.title: Hierarchies as tables
lessons.tip: PowerConnect imports a subset as a flat table with level columns, and the fact table should hold leaf values only.

exercises.q: How does a TM1 subset arrive in Power BI?
options: As a native Power BI hierarchy
As a flat table with level columns
exercises.explain: Level columns such as level000 and level001 trace each element's consolidation path.

exercises.q: The ___ column holds the top consolidation.
exercises.explain: level000 is the top consolidation; each deeper column is the next parent down.

exercises.q: Why keep the fact table at leaf level?
exercises.explain: TM1 consolidations are pre-aggregated, so including them counts every total twice.

exercises.q: Put the hierarchy dimension on the columns of the fact view.
exercises.explain: Put it on the rows, so its elements arrive as values in a single column.

exercises.q: Other dimensions can be pinned to one element, even a consolidation.
exercises.explain: Every other dimension should be at leaf level or pinned to a single element.

lessons.title: Make it roll up
lessons.tip: Fill blank levels, show descriptions, add the element as the deepest level, then relate the tables.

exercises.q: Use Table.___ to fill blank level columns.
exercises.explain: Table.ReplaceValue replaces empty level cells with the row's element name.

exercises.q: Put the steps in order
items: Load the hierarchy and fact tables
Fill in the blank level columns
Package the levels into a hierarchy
Relate the tables and build the visual
exercises.explain: These are the five steps to a hierarchy that rolls up correctly.

exercises.q: Deepest members collapse into their parent. What was skipped?
options: Adding the element as the deepest level
exercises.explain: Level columns hold only the parents, so add the element itself at the bottom.

exercises.q: Relate the tables on the aliased RegionName column.
exercises.explain: Relate them on the untouched Region key, one-to-many.

exercises.q: Match each term to its meaning
pairs: Click a bar to open a branch
exercises.explain: These pieces turn a flat subset into a hierarchy you can drill.

units.title: Security
units.objective: Apply TM1 security to Power BI reports with Row Level Security and secure data sources.
