sources.title: Securing datasets when using Power BI Service

lessons.title: TM1 security in Power BI
lessons.tip: PowerConnect turns your TM1 element security into Power BI Row Level Security.

exercises.q: PowerConnect turns TM1 permissions into what?
exercises.explain: It reads element-level security and group memberships and turns them into Row Level Security.

exercises.q: You must maintain a second security model in Power BI.
exercises.explain: Define access once in TM1; Power BI inherits it.

exercises.q: TM1 access changes reach Power BI on the next refresh.
exercises.explain: When someone joins, leaves or moves teams, it is reflected on the next refresh.

exercises.q: A regional manager and the CFO open the same dashboard. What happens?
options: Each sees only their permitted data
exercises.explain: The dashboard is shared once; each viewer's data is filtered by who they are.

exercises.q: Access decisions stay in ___, where they are already audited.
exercises.explain: Access stays governed and audited in TM1; Power BI inherits it.

lessons.title: Securing datasets
lessons.tip: In Desktop the user's own credentials apply, but Service refreshes run with administrator credentials.

exercises.q: Whose credentials does the connector use in Power BI Desktop?
exercises.explain: In Desktop the user's credentials are enforced when connecting to Planning Analytics.

exercises.q: Whose credentials do Power BI Service refreshes typically use?
exercises.explain: The Service data source usually has administrator credentials, so refreshes run as admin.

exercises.q: In self service, end users should not access the Service data source.
exercises.explain: This stops end users refreshing datasets with administrator credentials.

exercises.q: In self service, refreshes happen in Power BI ___.
exercises.explain: The custom connector in Desktop enforces TM1 security, then the report is published.

exercises.q: Some users see only Actuals, others Actuals and Budget. What can you do?
options: Set up a data source per portion
exercises.explain: Configure one data source per portion of data, each with the right credentials.

lessons.title: Row Level Security
lessons.tip: After joining the tables, add a role whose DAX filter matches the viewer to the }Clients column.

exercises.q: Put the RLS steps in order
items: Click Create and name the role
Pick the dimension table with element security
exercises.explain: Create a role, choose the secured dimension table, then add the DAX filter.

exercises.q: The DAX matches USERPRINCIPALNAME() against the }Clients column.
exercises.explain: LOOKUPVALUE finds security rows where }Clients equals USERPRINCIPALNAME().

exercises.q: The RLS expression uses the DAX function ___.
exercises.explain: The expression is built with LOOKUPVALUE on the security table.

exercises.q: RLS can only filter one dimension.
exercises.explain: You can configure DAX expressions for multiple dimensions.

exercises.q: By default, which column holds the elements in the dimension table?
exercises.explain: The element column is by default the first column of the table.

units.title: Publishing
units.objective: Publish reports to the Power BI Service and keep them refreshed from TM1 through a gateway.

sources.title: Publishing Reports to the Power BI Service

lessons.title: Refresh from the cloud
lessons.tip: Published dashboards stay connected to TM1 and refresh on demand or on a schedule.

exercises.q: Publishing to the Service gives a one-off snapshot of TM1 data.
exercises.explain: It is a live connection the Service can refresh on its own schedule.

exercises.q: Which Service feature keeps dashboards current automatically?
exercises.explain: Use the Service's own scheduled refresh to refresh on the cadence you choose.

exercises.q: You must open Power BI Desktop to refresh a published report.
exercises.explain: You can trigger a refresh from the cloud, with no need for Desktop.

exercises.q: Where can users open Service dashboards?
options: Any browser and the mobile app
exercises.explain: Service dashboards open in any browser and in the Power BI mobile app.

exercises.q: The Power BI Service is Microsoft's ___-hosted Power BI.
exercises.explain: The Power BI Service is the cloud-hosted version of Power BI.

lessons.title: Gateway and sharing
lessons.tip: Map the dataset to a PowerConnect gateway data source, then add users to the dataset roles.

exercises.q: Which rule applies to the gateway cluster?
exercises.explain: The gateway cluster has to be specific for PowerConnect.

exercises.q: Match each item to its role
pairs: Power BI Admin and TM1 admin
Maps the dataset to a data source
exercises.explain: A service account sets up the gateway; roles control who sees the dataset.

exercises.q: Put the gateway steps in order
items: Open the workspace with the report
exercises.explain: Find the dataset, map it to the gateway data source, then apply.

exercises.q: TM1 security changes apply when the dataset refreshes.
exercises.explain: Changed TM1 security is applied dynamically on the next dataset refresh.

exercises.q: To open the report, users need access to its ___.
exercises.explain: Users who want the report need permission on the underlying dataset.
